title: Temperature-Dependent Spin-Orbit Torque Generation in Perpendicularly Magnetized Topological Insulator-Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
authors: Soumyarup Hait, Benjamin A. Brereton, Ahmet Yagmur, Satoshi Sasaki, Gavin Burnell, Christopher H. Marrows
abstract: We report a comprehensive temperature-dependent investigation of spin-orbit torque (SOT) generation in heterostructures comprising a perpendicularly magnetized metallic multilayer grown on top of a topological insulator (TI) epilayer. Temperature-dependent second-harmonic Hall measurements reveal distinct trends in the magnitude of the spin-orbit torque across the studied heterostructures. Samples incorporating Bi2Se3 exhibit torques reaching approximately 12 mT/(10^12 A m^-2) at 15 K, around 5 times larger than those in a multilayer without the topological layer. The structure with a thin 2-nm Ta buffer for the multilayer shows the strongest enhancement and a pronounced increase at low temperatures, highlighting efficient spin-current generation from the topological surface states. In contrast, the sample with a 10 nm-thick Ta spacer exhibits reduced torque efficiency, consistent with partial attenuation of spin transmission through the buffer. Systems lacking Bi2Se3 but containing two heavy metals (Ta and Pt) yield significantly smaller torques, around 2.5 mT/(10^12 A m^-2), despite the presence of conventional spin Hall sources. These observations underscore the dominant role of TI-derived spin-momentum-locked currents in driving large damping-like torques and their sensitivity to interfacial structure and buffer-layer thickness.
summary: This work reports a detailed temperature-dependent investigation into Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) generation in $	ext{TI}/	ext{MML}$ heterostructures. By using second-harmonic Hall measurements, the authors demonstrate that spin currents originating from topological surface states significantly enhance SOT efficiency compared to conventional materials. The results underscore the critical role of interfacial engineering and low temperatures in maximizing spintronic device performance.
main_problem: The study investigates the temperature-dependent generation of spin-orbit torque (SOT) in advanced spintronic heterostructures to enable electrical manipulation of magnetization.
main_result: Topological insulator ($	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$)-derived currents dominate SOT generation, leading to significantly larger torques compared to conventional heavy metal sources, especially at low temperatures.
method: The research employs comprehensive temperature-dependent measurements using second-harmonic Hall voltage techniques and current shunting analysis to quantify spin-current contributions from different layers.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multilayer heterostructure stack consisting of a perpendicularly magnetized metallic multilayer (MML) grown on top of a topological insulator ($	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$) epilayer, separated by various buffer layers like Ta.
key_observables: SOT magnitude ($	au_{	ext{DL}}$), temperature dependence of torque, current shunting fractions ($f_{	ext{Bi}2	ext{Se}3}$, $f_{	ext{Ta}}$, $f_{	ext{MML}}$), Anomalous/Planar Hall Resistances.
important_parameters: Low temperatures (e.g., 15 K) show enhanced torque; thin Ta buffers (2 nm) maximize efficiency; the comparison between TI-containing and non-TI systems is key.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on decomposing the second-harmonic signal using azimuthal angle sweeps to separate contributions related to $	ext{B}_{	ext{DL}}$ and $	ext{B}_{	ext{FL}}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the heterostructure stack, temperature dependence of resistance/shunting fractions, and evolution of Hall resistances ($	ext{R}_{	ext{AHE}}$, $	ext{R}_{	ext{PHE}}$) with applied current.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system and measurement techniques (second-harmonic Hall measurements) to presenting quantitative results showing the enhancement provided by TIs, analyzing the role of buffer thickness, and concluding that TI-derived currents are dominant.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics rather than fundamental quantum dynamics, the study involves interfacial physics and spin transport phenomena which touch upon non-equilibrium many-body effects relevant to open quantum systems modeling.

(c) Optical micrograph of the Hall bar corresponding to the sample Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(2 nm)/MML.

Figure 2: Temperature dependent transport properties. (a) Temperature-dependent sheet resistance of the samples SiO2/Ta(2 nm)/MML, Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(2 nm)/MML, and Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(10 nm)/MML. (b–d) Fraction of the total current flowing through the Bi2Se3 (fBi2Se3),MML (fMML), and Ta buffer (fTa), respectively, as obtained from the parallel-resistor model, described in detail in the Supplementary Information. (d–f) Tem- perature dependence of the anomalous Hall resistance, and planar Hall resistance for the heterostructures.

Figure 3: Second harmonic Hall measurements. (a) Representative azimuthal-angle- dependent second-harmonic Hall signals for the Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(2 nm)/MML mea- sured at 25 K, 1.5 T, and an applied current of ∼9 mA. Black points denote the experimental data, while the red and blue dashed lines represent contributions to a fit to Eq. 1, from which the damping-like and field-like contributions (DLC and FLC) are extracted. Note the change of scale for the FLC contribution. (b–d) Magnetic-field dependence of DLC for the three samples, fitted using Eq. 2 to obtain the damping-like torque BDL and thermal contributions at different applied currents.

Figure 4: Damping-like contributions to the SOT. (a–c) Linear variation of the damping-like effective field BDL with applied current density for the Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(2 nm)/MML, Al2O3/Bi2Se3(20 nm)/Ta(10 nm)/MML, and SiO2/Ta(5 nm)/MML/Pt(4 nm) samples, respectively, measured at different temperatures. The points represent the BDL values extracted from the DLC-versus-field fits, while the solid lines are linear fits used to determine the damping-like torque per unit current density. (d) Temperature dependence of the extracted BDL per unit current density for all samples.
